newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler not opposed to job guarantees.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler not opposed to job guarantees.

text.p: Chrysler Corp President Robert Lutz said Wednesday the 95 percent job guarantees agreed to by Ford Motor Co in its new labor contract would not likely be a problem for Chrysler if it has the flexibiltiy to adjust workforce levels at individual plants.

Lutz, speaking to reporters at a convention for Chrysler dealers here, said he is "optimistic" the company will be able to reach an equitable settlement with the United Auto Workers union for a new labor contract covering the automaker's 66,000 hourly employees.

Lutz said maintaining jobs for 95 percent of its hourly workers over the past five years would not have caused a problem because Chrysler has added about 13,000 new hourly UAW jobs in the United States during that period.

In the future, he said Chrysler's ability to support a 95 percent employment guarantee would depend largely on contract language and Chrysler's flexibility to move employees from plant to plant in order to maintain efficiencies.
"If it's defined by little individual pockets and we have no ability to blend (workforces), that would be unacceptable," he said.
Lutz denied earlier statements by UAW President Stephen Yokich that Chrysler cares more about its suppliers than its workers, calling Yokich's statements "campaign rhetoric."
He said he has not heard whether Chrysler will be chosen as the second bargaining target by the UAW. The union reached a tentative deal with Ford September 16.
